newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rides U.S. products rally to firm finish.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rides U.S. products rally to firm finish.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended firmer on Thursday, propelled to session highs in the last couple of hours by a strong recovery in U.S. product markets, brokers said.
April Brent closed 30 cents higher at $19.70 a barrel after dipping as low as $19.16 in early dealing. It finished just below the intraday high of $19.78 a barrel.
"U.S. gasoline led the way this afternoon," said a broker.
"It has come out of hibernation and that seems to be what's rattling the market, although there's also some talk of colder weather returning to the U.S. Northeast," he added.
Private forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said temperatures in the region would average five degrees Fahrenheit below normal on Friday and stay low through the weekend.

Dealers said the bulls also took heart from the market's failure to break lower despite a raft of bearish news including rising supply from OPEC and non-OPEC producers and reduced crude throughput at some European refineries due to dismal margins.

British Petroleum (BP) became the latest European oil company to cut runs, trimming by about 12 percent throughput at its 400,000 bpd Nerefco refinery, a 65-35 joint venture with Texaco, industry sources said.
A BP spokesman could not confirm the reduction but said margins on refined products were being squeezed.
Earlier, IPE gas oil futures ended $2.75 a tonne firmer, catching the early ripples of New York's products-led rally.
March gas oil finished at $164.75 a tonne, just 25 cents off the session high, squeezing the prompt March/April contango by 50 cents to $1.50.
Firmer sentiment on products markets helped lift the Brent-gas oil crack, which ended at $2.78 a barrel from $2.31 on Wednesday.
